steps.statement: Joint rational coefficient constraints retain bounded differences.
steps.proof:
Fix a COMMON finite rational carrier Pi for actual REAL PA PC positive-growth gamma and finitely many actual relative REAL PA PC functions f_l. Shared-face rational equations and ALL-face PC nonnegative rational circuit inequalities apply separately to every entry. Reconstruct the support argument as in unreviewed272: generators of the whole tangent support include both lineality signs; K={lambda>=0:Ulambda=0} is a rational cone with finitely many positive circuit generators; germ PC is nonnegative costs on every generator. Local affine supports propagate along incident segments to give the printed PC inequalities, including real centers. This new application is not granted by a ledger.
For every cell sigma choose finite rational recession generators, including both lineality signs, and impose the RATIONAL equations d(f_l-gamma)(u)=0. These are exactly boundedness on each cell: an affine function is bounded on a polyhedron iff it vanishes on its recession cone. Indeed a nonempty rational polyhedron is a convex hull of a finite rational anchor set plus its finitely generated rational recession cone, after splitting lineality. Zero recession makes all affine values convex combinations of anchor values; the converse follows along x+t*u. Thus bounded PA coefficient differences on this FIXED carrier have a GLOBAL sup norm bound controlled by its finite anchors. The actual tuple lies in this joint rational polyhedral cone, with gamma positive growth given by finitely many strict recession evaluations. REAL cycle weights remain unchanged and do not enter these PC constraints.

steps.statement: Arbitrarily close exact convex rational decompositions of the entire tuple.
steps.proof:
Let z=(gamma,f_1,...,f_k) and let F be its minimal face in the JOINT cone. All active costs at z are exactly zero; their rational equalities give a rational affine hull. Inactive inequalities and the finite strict gamma-growth inequalities persist in a small relative neighborhood. For ANY delta>0 take a rational-coefficient simplex of vertices z_i=(gamma_i,f_1i,...,f_ki) there, each within delta of z, enclosing z in its relative interior. Start with a small enclosing simplex in the rational affine space and perturb vertices to rational points while preserving positive barycentric coordinates and all strict conditions. The zero-dimensional case is the unique rational point. Then z=sum t_i z_i EXACTLY, with real t_i>0 and sum t_i=1. EVERY component is rational-affine PA PC, gamma_i positive-growth, and EVERY f_li-gamma_i bounded by the exact recession equations.
This JOINT decomposition retains the SAME coefficients for gamma AND all f_l; decomposing gamma alone would not suffice. The bounded differences b_li=f_li-gamma_i converge UNIFORMLY ON ALL X to b_l=f_l-gamma as delta tends to zero, since their coefficient differences have zero recession and J1's fixed finite anchor sets control their norms. Arbitrary gamma_i-gamma need not be globally bounded, and that claim is never used.

steps.statement: Finite rational-wall maxima approximate the ACTUAL maximum globally.
steps.proof:
Set F_delta=sum_i t_i max_l f_li. Rational affine coefficients make every equality wall rational. A common finite rational refinement carries the finite maxima and their positive sum. Printed Jensen and monotonicity of max give PC at every real center. Its bounded relative difference is EXACTLY
 F_delta-gamma=sum_i t_i max_l(f_li-gamma_i)=sum_i t_i max_l b_li.
The true H=max_l f_l has H-gamma=max_l b_l and is continuous PC. It may have irrational walls and is NOT called rational-geometry PA. The one-Lipschitz maximum gives
 ||F_delta-H||_infty <=max_i,l ||b_li-b_l||_infty ->0.
This is GLOBAL and retains the actual reference; it does not require uniform approximation of gamma by references with different recession slopes. Jensen also gives F_delta>=max_l sum_i t_i f_li=H at EVERYpoint. Actual PA majorants are built BEFORE any operator/envelope is invoked. For errors <=2^(-n), adding the rational constant4*2^(-n) gives consecutive drops >=2^(-n-1), hence a genuine uniform decreasing PA regularization of H. No irrational maximum closure of finite PA was assumed.

steps.statement: Maximum closure of the actual approximation domain.
steps.proof: Define D_R(gamma) as the sup-norm closure of actual relative REAL PA PC functions; this definition assigns no operator. For arbitrary f_l in D choose simultaneous actual PA approximants a_ln with errors <=epsilon_n ->0. Apply J1-J3 to gamma and that finite tuple, obtaining actual relative PA PC h_n with ||h_n-max_l a_ln||<=epsilon_n. Then ||h_n-max_l f_l||<=2epsilon_n globally. Thus the finite maximum belongs to D_R(gamma) and max is jointly one-Lipschitz there. Common rational shifts give genuine decreasing regularization. This domain result does NOT depend on currently unaccepted272's MA extension. IF that extension is independently accepted, its operator applies to these genuine endpoints with the established raw mass/locality/fixed-C continuity. No operator is assigned outside D, and contact for general obstacles does not follow. Minima need not be PC.

steps.statement: Continuous convex scalar cap calculus as another actual-domain application.
steps.proof:
Let m=min_X gamma, finite by proper positive growth. If chi:[m,infinity)->R is convex, nondecreasing and chi(s)-s bounded, every secant slope is in[0,1], chi is one-Lipschitz, and chi(s)-s decreases to finite c_infinity. Extend chi constantly below m. There are finite continuous PA convex nondecreasing chi_n, with all breakpoint POSITIONS rational, slopes in[0,1], and slope exactly1 beyond a rational S_n, uniformly approximating chi on[m,infinity). Construct fine rational-node chord interpolants on a growing compact interval, then attach the slope-one line through the last value. Convexity preserves increasing chord slopes; above S_n the error is bounded by chi(S_n)-S_n-c_infinity. REAL nodal values/slopes are allowed; rational breakpoints give the geometry needed below.
Use J2 for gamma alone, with exact gamma=sum t_ni gamma_ni, rational gamma_ni and positive sum-one coefficients arbitrarily close in coefficients. A fixed small neighborhood has a COMMON positive-growth bound a*rho-b. For each n choose the vertices close enough that they uniformly approximate gamma on the compact region where some gamma_ni<=S_n. Define h_n=sum t_ni chi_n(gamma_ni). Each composed entry is REAL PA on rational geometry: rational breakpoints pull back by rational-affine gamma_ni. Convex nondecreasing composition preserves printed PC. Outside the common compact region every entry is on its slope-one branch, hence h_n=gamma+c_n; the target chi(gamma)-gamma differs from c_n only by the small tail error. On the compact region Lipschitzness plus sufficiently close coefficients gives uniform small error. Therefore h_n->chi(gamma) UNIFORMLY ON ALL X, every h_n-gamma bounded, and chi(gamma) is in the actual D_R(gamma), with a decreasing extraction. In particular max(gamma-j,-c) has a genuine actual-domain antecedent even when its walls are irrational; it is NOT finite rational-geometry PA. This does not authorize using that cap as a FINITE primitive divisor before extension: the height argument correctly uses rational gamma0 cutoffs first.

steps.statement: Explicit actual-reference maximum with irrational breakpoint and genuine raw limit.
steps.proof: On the saturated unit-weight line let A=sqrt2, c=1/sqrt3, gamma=A|x|, f=gamma and g=(A-1)|x|+max(|x|-1,0)+c. Both f and g are ACTUAL relative REAL PA PC on rational vertices0,+1,-1. Their maximum H=A|x|+(c-|x|)_+ has irrational breakpoints+/-c, so is not finite rational-geometry PA. For rational p_n<c<q_n in(0,1) with q_n-p_n->0 set lambda_n=(q_n-c)/(q_n-p_n) and h_n=A|x|+lambda_n(p_n-|x|)_++(1-lambda_n)(q_n-|x|)_+. These are actual relative REAL PA on rational vertices+/-p_n,+/-q_n. The central slope A-1>0 and positive outer jumps prove PC. The uniform error <=q_n-p_n follows from one-Lipschitz dependence on the cap parameter and exact lambda_n*p_n+(1-lambda_n)*q_n=c; convexity in that parameter gives h_n>=H. A joint rational tuple decomposition is explicit by also choosing rational A_-<A<A_+ with A_->1 and product barycentric weights on the(A,c)rectangle; summand recession differences cancel to give this same formula. Finite RAW primitive measures are2(A-1)delta_0+lambda_n(delta_p_n+delta_-p_n)+(1-lambda_n)(delta_q_n+delta_-q_n), total2A. Their weak C_b limit is2(A-1)delta_0+delta_c+delta_-c. Identification as MA(H) uses accepted S262 ALLcontinuousgraph theory for the actual real reference, AFTER this actual endpoint is established. No H-finite-PA assertion, moved reference, extra factorial or probability scaling. This illustrates J1-J4 rather than a new original graph solution.
